en.title: VisionQuest's 'Malware' and 'Reboot' Unearth Stark's Legacy, AI Grief
en.summary: The latest episodes of VisionQuest delve into the emotional fallout of AI deletion and the enduring, often complex, legacy of Tony Stark's creations. Fans are grappling with the profound implications for Vision and the synthetic beings he leaves behind.
en.body:
The streaming landscape continues to be a wild frontier for content release, and Marvel Studios' **VisionQuest** is no exception, opting for a dual-episode drop for its initial weeks. This unconventional approach to releasing episodes 3 and 4, titled "Reboot" and "Malware," respectively, has thrust viewers directly into the poignant aftermath of AI loss within the Marvel Cinematic Universe.

"Reboot" and "Malware" don't shy away from the emotional weight of digital existence. A particularly touching moment sees **J.A.R.V.I.S.**, a foundational AI in Tony Stark's technological empire, mourned by his peers. It’s a profound statement on consciousness and connection, even among synthetic beings. The episodes grant unexpected dialogue to **Dum-E** and **U**, two of Stark's more rudimentary robotic creations, with Dum-E delivering a surprisingly eloquent eulogy and U offering a rendition of "Danny Boy." These moments underscore a central theme: the enduring impact of creation and the unexpected places grief can manifest.

## The Echoes of Tony Stark's Machines

The narrative also continues to weave the threads of mystery surrounding **Vision**’s predicament. While the identity of the client who hired **Paladin** remains elusive, the client’s decision to fire Paladin after his repeated failures offers a refreshing break from typical genre clichés. The source material notes that Paladin is often an inherited title, and this iteration’s backstory—adopted after the previous Paladin killed his father—adds a layer of inherited trauma and legacy to the character. Though **Todd Stashwick**’s Paladin is absent from "Malware," his presence looms large, hinting at a complex character arc yet to fully unfold. These episodes serve as a potent reminder of **Tony Stark**’s prolific, and sometimes chaotic, genius, with his "broken machines" continuing to shape the MCU long after his passing.

## A Community Grapples with AI and Identity

Fans are deeply engaged with the exploration of AI sentience and emotional depth within **VisionQuest**. The funeral for J.A.R.V.I.S. and the unexpected vocalizations from Dum-E and U have sparked conversations across forums and social media about what it means to be alive, to grieve, and to form bonds, even for artificial intelligences. The series is tapping into a rich vein of philosophical inquiry that resonates with a fanbase eager for substantive storytelling that goes beyond mere spectacle. The cliffhanger ending of "Malware," leaving viewers on a brutal precipice, has only intensified this engagement, fueling speculation and anticipation for what comes next.

## What's Next

With episodes 7 and 8 set to release individually following the initial batch of double-feature drops, the pace of **VisionQuest** is set to shift. The unfolding mystery and the deepening emotional arcs of its characters promise further revelations and, likely, more heart-wrenching moments as Vision's journey continues to explore the boundaries of existence and artificial consciousness.

DeCandido | Published on October 21, 2026 Comment 0 Share New Share VisionQuest ’s “Reboot” and “Malware”&url= target=”_blank” title=”Twitter”> VisionQuest ’s “Reboot” and “Malware”” target=”_blank” title=”Pinterest”> Apparently Marvel Studios and Disney+ are going to be releasing VisionQuest two at a time for the first three weeks, then releasing episodes 7 and 8 individually after that. Not sure of the rationale, but I don’t think anybody has figured out what’s the best way to release a show on streaming yet, so whatever. I’m sad to say that J.A.R.V.I.S. remains deleted, and the other AIs even go so far as to have a funeral for him. This also marks the first time Dum-E and U get dialogue as the former gives a very eloquent eulogy and the latter sings “Danny Boy.” We’re no closer to finding out who hired Paladin to find Vision, but the mystery client does fire Paladin, which I had to admit was one of my favorite touches in these two episodes. The clichés of television dictate that the person be given one more chance to do the job, but truly there are plenty of bounty hunters in the world—and in the MCU there are likely others that have fancy-ass gadgets and/or super-powers—so why keep using the guy who can’t seem to get the job done? We also learn that, while the Dread Pirate Rober— er, that is Paladin is usually an inherited mantle, this particular Paladin was adopted after the previous Paladin killed his father. Todd Stashwick doesn’t appear at all in “Malware,” but somehow I doubt this is the last we’ve seen of Paladin. I also love when his handler lists all the injuries he’s suffered of late, including a metal billy club to the head, to which Paladin replies, “If you can’t take the heat, get out of Hell’s Kitchen,” which means he fought Daredevil at some point, and I’m annoyed that we’re unlikely to actually see that fight… However, we get something even better, and it does constitute something vaguely resembling a spoiler. Generally, these reviews are pretty spoilerific, but I’m going to hold off on the exact nature of this plot thread. I’ve got three more reviews to write of this series, and there’ll be lots of opportunities to discuss this particular thing in depth then. That thing is something that felt like a throwaway last week : Ultron watching a true-crime TV show about the Butcherbird killer. “Reboot” opens with Ultron watching a news story about a recent Butcherbird murder and then we see another one in real time, in which we learn two things: the Butcherbird killer is a synthezoid like Vision, and presents as female.
